findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, House second reading, passed 66-47
findings.note: Kiger is listed among the Ayes. The final enrolled bill includes a rule that a voter registration application is processed only if it affirmatively states the applicant is a U.S. citizen, with a notice and sworn-statement step if the citizenship question is left blank. Other parts cover ballot challenges, audits and overseas voters.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, House concurrence in Senate committee substitute, 62-47
findings.note: Kiger is listed among the Ayes on the final House vote. The Governor vetoed the bill on 8/17/2026; no override vote appears in the bill history as of the page I read.

findings.motion: HB 958 ratified text, Section 2.4(c), new G.S. 163-83 requirement for citizenship on voter registration applications
findings.note: Text of the bill Kiger voted for. Says: the county board processes a registration only if the application affirmatively indicates the applicant is a citizen; if the answer is blank, the board sends a notice and a form to be signed under penalty of perjury, to be returned within 30 days. This ratified text contains no photo-ID section.
